name: Ts'ün-Lao
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul (ed.). 2009. Ethnologue, 16th ed., entry 'Ts'ün-Lao' (tsl); also 17th ed. (2014) and 22nd ed. (2019) entries, the Internet Archive copies.
sources.note: Nothing; identity record only: 'A language of Viet Nam.. Population 10,000 (1993 Dang Nghiem Van). Region Northwest, Lai Chau Province. Alternate names Lao. Classification Tai-Kadai, Kam-Tai, Be-Tai, Tai-Sek, Tai, Central. Comments Official ethnic community, with associated names Lào Bóc and Lào Noi.'

sources.citation: Strecker, David. 1985. The classification of the Caolan languages. In Suriya Ratanakul, David Thomas & Suwilai Premsrirat (eds.), Southeast Asian Linguistic Studies Presented to André-G. Haudricourt, 479-492. Bangkok: Mahidol University.
sources.note: Nothing (a full-text search for stress/accent / accent: 0 hits). Comparative-classification paper: argues that Ts'ün-wa (the language of the Ts'ün-lao), Caolan and Nung-an of NE Vietnam are ?Yai (Northern Tai) languages that share areal cluster developments with Tay-Nung. Note p. 489: 'Haudricourt (1960, sections 19, 28) says that the people are called Ts'ün-lao "villagers" ("habitants des hameaux") and the language is called Ts'ün-wa. These are apparently Chinese names'.
sources.venue: Southeast Asian Linguistic Studies Presented to André-G

sources.citation: Haudricourt, André-G. 1960 [Glottolog: 1961]. V. Note sur les dialectes de la région de Moncay. Bulletin de l'École française d'Extrême-Orient 50(1): 161-177. DOI 10.3406/befeo.1960.1519.
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative wordlist / historical-phonology note (initials, tone correspondences) on Yao, Tai ('thô' and the two 'Ts'un-wa' informants of the Ts'un-lao) and Chinese dialects of the Móng Cái region; a full-text search for stress/accent / tonique / intensité gives 0 hits.
